name: Nathan
bio:
Nathan was a prophet in David's court who delivered the LORD's covenant promise that David's throne would be established forever, and who later became the courageous voice that confronted the king over his sin with Bathsheba.

## 📖 Core Story: Carrying the Davidic Covenant

When David, now settled in his cedar palace, told Nathan he wished to build a house for the ark of God, Nathan at first answered on his own initiative, "Go, do all that is in your heart, for the LORD is with you" (2 Samuel 7:1-3). That same night, however, the word of the LORD came to Nathan and corrected his answer: David himself would not build a house for the LORD, but the LORD would instead build a house — a dynasty — for David. God promised to raise up David's offspring after him, establish his kingdom, and make his throne secure forever, while directing that it would be this son, not David, who would build the temple (2 Samuel 7:4-16). Nathan faithfully reported "all these words" and "this whole vision" to David exactly as he received them, even though it reversed his own earlier counsel (2 Samuel 7:17) — a telling picture of a prophet who would speak only what the LORD gave him, not merely what seemed wise or pleasing in the moment. David's prayer of humble gratitude in response closes out the chapter, a high point in his reign and in the Bible's unfolding promise of a lasting throne.

## 📖 Core Story: Confronting the King Over Bathsheba and Uriah

After David arranged Uriah's death to cover his affair with Bathsheba, the LORD sent Nathan to confront him. Rather than accuse David outright, Nathan told him a parable: a rich man with vast flocks had taken a poor man's one beloved ewe lamb — his only possession, raised like a daughter — to feed a guest, rather than take from his own abundant flock. David's anger blazed, and he declared the man deserved to die and should repay the lamb fourfold, having shown no pity (2 Samuel 12:1-6). Nathan then delivered the verdict David had just pronounced on himself: "You are the man!" He laid out everything the LORD had given David — anointing, deliverance from Saul, the house of Israel and Judah — and asked why David had despised the LORD's command to kill Uriah and take his wife. Nathan pronounced the LORD's judgment: the sword would never leave David's house, and calamity would be raised against him from within his own household (2 Samuel 12:7-12). When David confessed simply, "I have sinned against the LORD," Nathan answered that the LORD had taken away his sin and he would not die — but because of the great contempt David's act had shown the LORD's enemies, the son born of the affair would die (2 Samuel 12:13-14). Nathan's unflinching courage in confronting the most powerful man in Israel to his face, armed with nothing but a story and the word of the LORD, stands as one of Scripture's boldest examples of prophetic integrity.

After the child's death, David comforted Bathsheba, and she bore another son; David named him Solomon, but the LORD loved the child and sent word through Nathan that he should be called Jedidiah, "beloved of the LORD" (2 Samuel 12:24-25).

## 📖 Core Story: Securing Solomon's Succession

Many years later, as David lay old and feeble, his son Adonijah declared himself king without David's knowledge, backed by Joab and the priest Abiathar. Nathan went to Bathsheba and warned her that she and Solomon would be in mortal danger if Adonijah's bid succeeded, coaching her to remind David of his earlier oath that Solomon would reign after him; Nathan then came in right behind her and confirmed her report to the king (1 Kings 1:11-27). David swore on the spot that Solomon would be made king that day, and it was Zadok and Nathan together who anointed Solomon at Gihon amid great public celebration, decisively ending Adonijah's attempt before it could take hold (1 Kings 1:28-40). Nathan's final act in Scripture thus mirrors his first: just as he once delivered God's promise of an everlasting throne to David, he now ensured that promise reached the right son.
